thread.title: Streaming roundup: Apple goes to Hollywood… Quebec could tax Netflix

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Streaming roundup: Apple goes to Hollywood… Quebec could tax Netflix
text: – Staff Writer, L.A. Biz Mar 29, 2018, 5:48pm PDT Streaming services such as Netflix Inc. (NASDAQ: NFLX), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN), Hulu — a joint venture among The Walt Disney Co. (NYSE: DIS), 21st Century Fox (NASDAQ: FOXA, FOX), Comcast (NASDAQ: CMCSA)-owned NBCUniversal and Time Warner Inc. (NYSE: TWX) — and others have transformed the entertainment landscape. Here are recent stories on the streaming industry reported by The Business Journals and elsewhere: Major League Soccer gambles on local digital play This year’s most intriguing local media rights deals did not start out as the traditional ones do, but their implications already are quickly changing the way leagues and teams view their local rights. Take YouTube TV’s recent deal with the MLS expansion team LAFC. Executives with MLS, LAFC and YouTube TV were at the tail end of negotiating a jersey sponsorship deal when league executives broached the idea of adding the team’s local media rights to the deal. ( New York Business Journal ) BAMTech’s NHL GM seeks product innovations Whitney Howard, a music fanatic, joined BAMTech in July following a nearly 20-year career that has taken her from Wall Street to Hollywood, to most recently her home state of South Carolina — where she was teaching high school math. She found herself on the road again back to New York after being handpicked by BAMTech CEO Michael Paull to oversee the company’s relationship with the NHL. ( New York Business Journal ) Amazon reportedly set to spend $1 billion on sci-fi series Amazon Studios wants to create a show that's as buzzworthy as "Game of Thrones" and reportedly plans to acquire the rights to a popular Chinese book series, "The Three-Body Problem." Rights for the 2008 sci-fi novel by Liu Cixin could sell for $1 billion. ( Bizwomen ) U.S. TV ad spending to fall in 2018 TV ad spending will continue its decline this year, according to eMarketer’s latest U.S. advertising forecast. With cord-cutting accelerating and over-the-top (OTT) viewing on the rise, outlays on TV ads will slip 0.5 percent in 2018 to $69.87 billion. Meanwhile, total digital ad spending in the U.S. will climb 18.7 percent this year to $107.30 billion. ( eMarketer ) Netflix, Amazon face retail sales tax crackdown in Quebec Quebec is getting serious about taxing Amazon.com Inc. and Netflix Inc. Canada’s second-most populous province said Tuesday it would make the collection of the provincial sales tax mandatory for suppliers of goods and services based outside Quebec to put them on par with local rivals. ( Bloomberg ) Endeavor buys streaming provider NeuLion for $250 million Endeavor, the holding company formerly known as WME-IMG, has acquired streaming technology firm NeuLion for $250 million, the companies announced Monday. NeuLion powers the video delivery of a wide range of content owners, particularly major sports leagues. Endeavor owns some of those leagues as well, including UFC and Professional Bull Riders as part of an effort to diversify the company beyond the core talent agency business. ( Variety ) Apple goes to Hollywood. Will its story have a happy ending? Known for its bold designs and its big marketing campaigns, Apple Inc . (NASDAQ: AAPL) relishes its status as a dominant force in the corporate world. So it was noteworthy when one of its executives, Eddy Cue, struck a note of humility during a discussion this month at the South by Southwest conference in Austin, Texas. “We don’t know anything about making television,” said Mr. Cue, a senior vice president who oversees the team in charge of the company’s original programming initiative. ( New York Times )
